title: introduce-sustained-throughput-allocator-and-degradation-buffer
author: Aisha Kumar
release_notes: Add sustained-throughput allocator with degradation buffer to improve per-tenant throughput guarantees and reduce reactive scaling churn. Exposes telemetry for 1/5/50/95 utilization percentiles and a new diagnostics endpoint.
description:
Motivation: production tenants have highly variable short-term bursts but care most about sustained throughput guarantees over 30s-5m windows. Current autoscaler reacts to instantaneous utilization and causes spiky scale events that either overshoot cost or violate per-tenant throughput SLOs. This PR introduces a sustained-throughput-allocator (STA) plus a degradation-buffer to smooth decisions and prioritize long-running commitments over transient bursts.

Design summary: the allocator maintains a per-tenant EWMA of allocated throughput and a separate sustained-window estimator (configurable: default 60s, can be tuned per-tenant). Allocation decisions use a two-tier policy: (1) commit floor: ensure committed minimum throughput when sustained demand exceeds floor; (2) elastic buffer: allow short bursts using a shared degradation-buffer that decays over time if unused. The degradation-buffer is a time-decoupled pool that absorbs transient demand without immediately increasing reserved capacity. If sustained demand persists beyond buffer decay, allocator triggers normal provisioning.

Key behaviors and constraints:
- Respect existing reservation contracts and percentiles (no contract changes).
- Use conservative ramping (max +25% allocation per 30s) to avoid oscillation.
- Default safety: if per-tenant EWMA drops sharply, degrade tenant throughput softly over a grace window instead of abrupt eviction.
- Backwards compatible control-plane flags to enable/disable per-tenant sustained windows and buffer-sharing.

Telemetry and observability: new metrics exported to console: "sustained_demand_ewma", "degradation_buffer_level", "allocated_floor", "elastic_allocations", and percentile sketches for tenant utilization (p01/p05/p50/p95). Added a diagnostics endpoint (/debug/allocator/{tenant}) returning current state (read-only, auth-guarded) for on-call troubleshooting.

Implementation notes:
- core allocator implementation: server/autoscaler/sta_allocator.go (controller + reconciliation loop)
- buffer manager: server/autoscaler/degradation_buffer.go
- proto/contract changes: api/autoscale/v1/allocator.proto (adds optional sustained_window_ms and buffer_enabled flags)
- telemetry: observability/metrics/collector.go (adds sketches)
- tests: server/autoscaler/sta_allocator_test.go (unit + integration test harness using synthetic load profiles)

Rollout plan: staged rollout via feature flag:
- Canary on 10% of traffic (non-critical tenants) with metric guards for error increase, latency, and cost uplift.
- Expand to Dedicated fleets after 48h of stable metrics.
- Force-off via operator if degradation_buffer_level shows negative drift or sustained evictions spike.

Checklist: [x] unit tests added [x] integration harness scenarios added [x] console dashboards updated [x] Linear ENG-3214 linked [ ] documentation page (follow-up small PR)

Related: builds on ideas from ENG-2120 (graceful-headroom) but focuses on time-decoupled buffer semantics and sustained-window guarantees.

Impact: reduces autoscaler churn on observed customer workloads, improves 99th percentile sustained throughput stability for tenants with long-running background requests, and decreases transient over-provisioning by sharing elastic capacity across tenants.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice approach. Two questions: (1) how do we prevent starvation when many tenants simultaneously exploit the degradation buffer? (2) can we bound the buffer's cross-tenant lending to avoid SLA drift?

Aisha Kumar: For (1) the buffer manager enforces per-tenant lend caps and an aggregate safety threshold that triggers progressive denial. For (2) yes — buffer uses configurable per-tenant weight and an absolute cap per pool; defaults are conservative and documented in deploy/featureflags.yaml.
Priya Nair: Please add a canary metric that alerts if per-tenant tail latency increases >5% during rollout. Also, add an e2e scenario where sustained load persists beyond decay window.
Aisha Kumar: Added canary metric (alloc_tail_latency_increase_pct) and extended integration harness with a 10-minute sustained load profile in sta_allocator_test.go.
Evan Lee: left a small nit in sta_allocator.go around context cancellation handling in the decay loop; recommend early return to avoid noisy logs.
Aisha Kumar: fixed the cancellation path and added a unit test to assert proper shutdown without spurious logs.
merge_summary: Merged by Priya Nair on 2025-02-05 via squash merge. Merge commit: squash of 4 commits into main. Post-merge: created a follow-up ticket ENG-3378 for docs and a rollout checklist. No rollbacks required during canary.
